content: Hope is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul.
author: Emily Dickinson
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

Across his life and work, Emily Dickinson saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: What defensive wall or grudge are you holding onto that is keeping genuine warmth and intimacy away?

originalQuote: Hope is the Thing with Feathers— / That Perches in our Soul— / And sings the Tune without the words— / And never stops—at all— / And sweetest in the Gale is heard; / And sore must be the Storm / That could abash the little Bird / That kept so many warm— / And a safe Sound!
